417: func runtimeEventDraft(req runtimepkg.Request, event runtimepkg.Event) runcontrol.EventDraft {
418: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
419: 	lowerType := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Type))
420: 	lowerKind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Kind))
421: 	switch lowerType {
422: 	case "warning", "warn", "error":
423: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
424: 	case "artifact", "file":
425: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventArtifact
426: 	case "finding":
427: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventFinding
428: 	case "message", "text", "output", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text", "reasoning", "content", "delta":
429: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
430: 	default:
431: 		// Kind-based fallback: reasoning and message kinds should be visible as message, not coalesced progress.
432: 		switch lowerKind {
433: 		case "message", "reasoning", "assistant", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text":
434: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
435: 		case "tool", "tool_use", "tool_call", "tool_call_update":
436: 			// Tools stay as progress but with distinct payload so coalescing can distinguish.
437: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventProgress
438: 		}
439: 	}
440: 	payload := map[string]string{
441: 		"runtime_event_id": boundedSafe(event.ID),
442: 		"runtime_run_id":   boundedSafe(event.RunID),
443: 		"session_id":       boundedSafe(event.SessionID),
444: 		"type":             boundedSafe(event.Type),
445: 		"kind":             boundedSafe(event.Kind),
446: 	}
447: 	if lowerKind == "tool" || lowerKind == "tool_use" || lowerKind == "tool_call" || lowerKind == "tool_call_update" {
448: 		captureToolObservation(payload, event.Payload)
449: 	}
450: 	// Preserve safe observable payload fields into durable storage for observability.
451: 	// Deny sensitive keys and truncate values to runcontrol-safe limits.
452: 	// Flatten one level of nesting so tool/action names buried in maps are surfaced as top-level payload keys
453: 	// that the run timeline JS expects (payload.tool, payload.action, payload.title, etc.).
454: 	for key, value := range event.Payload {
455: 		if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
456: 			continue
457: 		}
458: 		normalized := strings.TrimSpace(key)
459: 		if normalized == "" || len(normalized) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(normalized, "\x00\r\n") {
460: 			continue
461: 		}
462: 		if normalized == "type" || normalized == "kind" {
463: 			continue
464: 		}
465: 		if nested, ok := value.(map[string]any); ok {
466: 			for subKey, subVal := range nested {
467: 				if isSensitivePayloadKey(subKey) {
468: 					continue
469: 				}
470: 				subNorm := strings.TrimSpace(subKey)
471: 				if subNorm == "" || len(subNorm) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(subNorm, "\x00\r\n") {
472: 					continue
473: 				}
474: 				if _, exists := payload[subNorm]; exists {
475: 					continue
476: 				}
477: 				// Promote common observable sub-keys; namespace the rest to avoid collisions.
478: 				promote := map[string]bool{"tool": true, "title": true, "detail": true, "text": true, "delta": true, "content": true, "message": true, "action": true, "state": true, "status": true, "native_type": true, "line": true}
479: 				targetKey := subNorm
480: 				if !promote[subNorm] {
481: 					targetKey = normalized + "_" + subNorm
482: 					if len(targetKey) > 128 {
483: 						continue
484: 					}
485: 				}
486: 				if _, exists := payload[targetKey]; exists {
487: 					continue
488: 				}
489: 				str := payloadValueString(subVal)
490: 				if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
491: 					continue
492: 				}
493: 				if len(payload) >= 30 {
494: 					break
495: 				}
496: 				payload[targetKey] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
497: 			}
498: 			// Also keep a compact stringified top-level for debugging if not promoted.
499: 			if len(payload) < 30 {
500: 				if _, exists := payload[normalized]; !exists {
501: 					str := payloadValueString(value)
502: 					if strings.TrimSpace(str) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(str, "[map omitted") {
503: 						payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
504: 					}
505: 				}
506: 			}
507: 			continue
508: 		}
509: 		str := payloadValueString(value)
510: 		if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
511: 			continue
512: 		}
513: 		if len(payload) >= 30 {
514: 			break
515: 		}
516: 		if _, exists := payload[normalized]; exists {
517: 			continue
518: 		}
519: 		payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
520: 	}
521: 	// Ensure the most useful display keys are always present even if nested.
522: 	for _, want := range []string{"tool", "action", "title", "detail", "text", "delta"} {
523: 		if _, ok := payload[want]; ok {
524: 			continue
525: 		}
526: 		if v := findNestedString(event.Payload, want); v != "" {
527: 			payload[want] = boundedPayloadValue(v)
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	omission := (*runcontrol.Omission)(nil)
531: 	if event.RawPresent || event.RawOmitted {
532: 		reason := firstSafeValue(event.RawOmissionReason, "runtime payload omitted by safe persistence policy")
533: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe(reason), Count: 1}
534: 	} else if len(event.Payload) > len(payload)-5 {
535: 		// Payload had more fields than we persisted (truncated/omitted keys) – record for diagnostics but don't hide persisted fields.
536: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe("runtime payload truncated to safe observable fields"), Count: 1}
537: 	}
538: 	return runcontrol.EventDraft{
539: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeRuntime,
540: 		Stage: boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]), Task: boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"])),
541: 		Kind: payload["kind"], Tool: payload["tool"], Action: payload["action"],
542: 		Reason: payload["reason"], Detail: firstSafeValue(payload["detail"], payload["title"]),
543: 		Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
544: 	}
545: }

547: func isSensitivePayloadKey(key string) bool {
548: 	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
549: 	for _, marker := range []string{"secret", "token", "password", "authorization", "cookie", "api_key", "apikey", "credential", "auth"} {
550: 		if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
551: 			return true
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 	return false

metadata.output:
```text
workspace-scoped run ID
operation kind and project/study/sprint/stage target
accepted / queued / running / terminal lifecycle timestamps
attempt, stage, task, agentwrap run/session, process, and external-harness correlations
owner identity, renewable lease, heartbeat, fencing value, and safe process-birth identity
latest durable event sequence and retention boundary
cancellation request/acknowledgement facts
one immutable arbitrated terminal result or explicit cleanup uncertainty
safe diagnostics, schema version, and migration metadata
```

Acceptance of a runtime-backed execution is atomic with durable run creation and happens before child execution. If required acceptance persistence fails, the child does not start. Event records are redacted before persistence, assigned monotonically increasing per-run sequences, and committed before live fan-out. The store may compact detail, but it must retain an explicit snapshot and lower replay boundary so clients can distinguish complete replay from a gap.

Active-run queries are workspace-wide. Product-page status may filter the common projection, but the global running count cannot be derived from the current page, browser session, or one server's memory. Planning stage readiness and operational execution lifecycle are separate types; UI code must not infer `running` from a stage-status enum that cannot represent it.

Read visibility is independent from originating-session continuity. Mutation still requires fresh authorization and a resolvable current owner. Cancellation is idempotent, durably recorded, routed through the canonical product/runtime cancellation path, and arbitrated against completion, failure, timeout, interruption, shutdown, and reconciliation so only one terminal outcome wins.

Liveness is conservative. A PID alone is insufficient because of PID reuse. Lease expiry, missing process, missing owner, artifact presence, or lost server memory cannot independently prove completion. Reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent stale-writer protection, records its evidence and decisions, and exposes `stalled`, `interrupted`, or `cleanup_uncertain` where truth cannot be proven.

The following are required reasoning decisions, not preselected implementation requirements:

- same-host multi-process versus shared-filesystem multi-host support and the guarantees at that boundary
- dedicated coordinator/daemon, fenced direct repository writers, or a hybrid
- filesystem snapshot/journal, SQLite, agentwrap store composition, or another smallest sufficient durable mechanism
- interface/package ownership without moving workflow semantics out of study/sprint modules or duplicating agentwrap
- Timestamp.
- Level.
- Command.
- Workspace.
- Study.
- Project.
- Sprint.
- Run ID.
- Run schema version.
- Owner and fencing identity when applicable.
- Task ID.
- Stage/execution ID.
- Attempt.
- Runtime.
- Model.
- Event type.
- Message.
- Agentwrap run ID.
- Agentwrap session ID.
- Agentwrap event kind.
- Agentwrap policy decision when applicable.
- Durable event sequence and replay boundary when applicable.

## 25. Migration From Prototype

The Go implementation must preserve the important prototype workflows:

- Study listing.
- Study initialization.
- Single dimension/source run.
- Full study run.
- Stateful run-loop.
- Status.
- Synthesis.
- Summary.
- Code extraction.
- Project catalog validation.
- Sprint planning flow through `plan`.
- Sprint execute flow through `execute`.
- Sprint automated review through root `review.md`.
- Sprint deep-smoke summary through root `smoke.md` with detailed evidence retained in the external harness.
- CLI/TUI operation of review, smoke, focused reruns, cancellation, evidence inspection, and recovery.
- Markdown document sources with `applicable_dimensions`.

The Go implementation may intentionally change:

- Command grouping for clarity.
- Config file format.
- Internal state schema.
- Runtime adapter implementation.
- Validation strictness.
- Logging format.

The Go implementation must intentionally change runtime execution from prototype-owned OpenCode process management to agentwrap-owned runtime supervision.

Migration support should include:

- Ability to read existing study directory layouts where practical.
- Validation command that reports incompatible or missing files.
- Documentation for converting prototype config into `ultraplan.yml`.
- Documentation for removing/replacing manual `review.md` and legacy `deep-smoke.md` with the Phase 3 generated `review.md` and `smoke.md`.
- Validation that recognizes legacy artifacts without treating them as current Phase 3 evidence.

## 26. Acceptance Criteria

UltraPlan Go is technically acceptable when:

- `go test ./...` passes.
- CLI builds as a single binary.
- `ultraplan --help` and command help are complete.
- Workspace init and validation work.
- Study init from YAML creates expected structure.
- Source discovery finds directories and top-level Markdown document sources.
- Markdown source `applicable_dimensions` filters source/dimension task creation and validation.
- Study list commands work.
- Single fake-runtime analysis writes and validates a report.
- Runtime execution uses `github.com/Antonio7098/agentwrap` and the `agentwrap/opencode` adapter.
- Default runtime composition includes `ObservingRuntime`, `ValidatingRuntime`, and `PolicyRunner`.

21:

28: 	NewAttemptID() (AttemptID, error)
29: }
30: 
31: // RandomIDSource reads 128 bits from Reader for every generated identity.
32: // Reader defaults to crypto/rand.Reader.
33: type RandomIDSource struct {
34: 	Reader io.Reader
35: }

38: 	id, err := s.generate("run_")
39: 	if err != nil {
40: 		return "", err
41: 	}
42: 	return RunID(id), nil
43: }

47: 	if err != nil {
48: 		return "", err
49: 	}
50: 	return AttemptID(id), nil
51: }

53: func (s RandomIDSource) generate(prefix string) (string, error) {
54: 	reader := s.Reader
55: 	if reader == nil {
56: 		reader = rand.Reader
57: 	}
58: 	raw := make([]byte, randomIDBytes)
59: 	if _, err := io.ReadFull(reader, raw); err != nil {
60: 		return "", wrapError(CodeUnavailable, "generate_id", "secure random identity generation failed", true, err)
61: 	}
62: 	return prefix + strings.ToLower(idEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)), nil
63: }

65: func (id RunID) Validate() error {
66: 	return validateOpaqueID(string(id), "run_", "run_id")
67: }

70: 	return validateOpaqueID(string(id), "att_", "attempt_id")
71: }
72: 
73: func validateOpaqueID(value, prefix, field string) error {
74: 	if len(value) != len(prefix)+encodedIDBytes || !strings.HasPrefix(value, prefix) {
75: 		return invalidField(field, "must be an opaque "+prefix+" base32 128-bit identifier")
76: 	}
77: 	encoded := value[len(prefix):]
78: 	if encoded != strings.ToLower(encoded) {
79: 		return invalidField(field, "must use canonical lowercase base32")
80: 	}

82: 	if err != nil || len(raw) != randomIDBytes {
83: 		return invalidField(field, "must contain exactly 128 bits of canonical base32 data")
84: 	}
85: 	if canonical := strings.ToLower(idEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)); canonical != encoded {

# Recovery Runbook

Runtime success is not product success. Treat a run as complete only when required artifacts exist and validation passes.

## First Checks

Run:

```bash
ultraplan health
ultraplan study <study> status
ultraplan study <study> validate
```

Use `--json` for automation:

```bash
ultraplan health --json
ultraplan study <study> status --json
ultraplan study <study> validate --json
```

## Validation Failures

If validation fails:

1. Read the failed check, observed value, path, and guidance.
2. Inspect the named artifact.
3. Repair the source artifact or rerun the affected task.
4. Run validation again.

Do not treat a runtime-completed task as complete when the expected report is missing or invalid.

## Missing Artifacts

Common missing artifacts include per-source reports, final reports, `summary.csv`, and `.ultraplan/run-state.json`.

- Missing per-source report: rerun `study <study> run <dimension> <source>` or resume with `run-loop`.
- Missing final report: rerun `study <study> synthesize <dimension>` after source reports validate.
- Missing summary: run `study <study> summary`.
- Missing run state: start `study <study> run-loop` to create durable state, or use `run-all` for a non-resumable batch.

Planning artifacts use a separate chain under `projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/`. Missing planning artifacts should be repaired stage by stage:

- Missing `requirements.md`: run `sprint <project> <sprint> prompt requirements` to inspect roadmap/docs context, then `sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to requirements`.
- Missing or invalid `code-context.md`: validate requirements and the configured implementation target, inspect `prompt code-context`, then run `flow --to code-context`. A successful rerun atomically replaces only `code-context.md`; runtime failure, cancellation, validation failure, or promotion/state failure preserves the last valid artifact.
- Missing `sprint-index.md`: run `sprint <project> <sprint> prompt sprint-index` to inspect context, then `sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to sprint-index`.
- Missing `technical-handbook.md`: validate `sprint-index` first, then run `flow --to technical-handbook`.
- Missing `reasoning.md`: validate area reasoning inputs if selected, then run `flow --to reasoning`.
- Missing `plan.md`: validate `reasoning`, then run `flow --to plan`.
- Missing `flow-state.json`: run `sprint <project> <sprint> status` to refresh artifact state.

If a downstream stage reports `invalid_path`, `containment`, `file_kind`, `missing_source`, `invalid_range`, `changed_during_read`, `invalid_encoding`, or `budget_exceeded`, repair or regenerate the reference-only context pack and rerun the affected stage. UltraPlan does not silently omit or truncate selected evidence. The shared prefix is rebuilt from current files on each top-level operation; browser reconnect/restart recovers readiness and the latest durable outcome from sprint state rather than retaining prompt bytes in the web process.

If stage skills are missing or stale, preview and rematerialise them:

```bash
ultraplan skills materialise all --dry-run
ultraplan skills materialise all
```

Customized skill files are preserved unless overwrite is confirmed. Use
`--force` only when the embedded versions should replace those customizations.
After an agent writes or repairs a planning artifact, run `sprint status
--json`; status persists the derived stage state while preserving review and
smoke evidence. Do not hand-edit state JSON to mark a stage complete.

The governed sprint chain continues through execute, review, and smoke using the shared `sprint verify` transition. Verification does not authorize issue management, remediation, or agent-driven Git mutation. Configured stage publication runs only after canonical validation and persistence.

## Verify Recovery

- Interrupted review: run `sprint <project> <sprint> status` to inspect completed coverage and retained sessions, then rerun `review`, `verify`, or `flow`. Compatible attempts resume by default.
- Intentional fresh review: use `review --restart`, `verify --restart-review`, or `flow --restart-review`. Restart cannot be combined with focused review.
- Changed review inputs or model: the saved attempt is incompatible and the next review starts fresh automatically.
- Expired running attempt: `sprint status` derives an attempt that has lacked a terminal update for more than 24 hours as timed out without mutating state; the next explicit review/smoke operation owns the durable transition.
- Review failure: resolve findings and rerun review. Use `--force-review --override-reason <text> --yes` only for diagnostic smoke; it cannot promote review or the overall assessment.
- Smoke interruption or timeout: confirm no harness process remains, inspect external run evidence, then rerun `verify --to smoke --yes` or the explicit `smoke --yes` action.
- Fresh canonical review with stale smoke: rerun the required containing smoke suite; a narrow diagnostic selection does not replace containing-suite evidence.

## Smoke Recovery

- `smoke review_gate`: regenerate a missing, malformed, or stale review. Use `--force-review` only for a current fail/blocked diagnostic run.
- `smoke protocol` or `containment`: repair the cataloged protocol-v1 manifest, executable, cwd, or evidence roots; never infer commands from README prose.
- `smoke timeout`, `cancellation`, or `cleanup`: inspect external evidence, confirm owned descendants are gone, and retry with a bounded timeout. The previous valid `smoke.md` remains current until validation marks it stale.
- `smoke evidence`: restore immutable run/issue evidence or rerun the sufficient suite. Do not copy raw evidence into the sprint.
- `reconciliation required`: `smoke.md` committed but flow state did not. Validate both files and rerun smoke to reconcile; automatic recovery is deferred.
- stale or missing evidence: `sprint status` and `validate smoke` must be treated as non-passing until a new evidence-backed run is committed.

## Stale Running Tasks

`study status` shows active, retrying, waiting, failed, cancelled, and recent tasks from persisted run state. If tasks appear stuck:

1. Check whether an UltraPlan process is still running.
2. Check lock diagnostics in `study status`.
3. Confirm runtime/provider state outside UltraPlan if a task is still active.
4. Resume with `study <study> run-loop` only after deciding the previous process is gone or safe to abandon. Continuing shared study progress is the default. Use `--reset` only when you intentionally want to archive and rebuild progress.

## Browser Operation Recovery

The browser's operation handle, event replay, confirmation, and subscriber are
bounded, ephemeral views. Product-owned workspace/run state is authoritative.

- Refresh, navigation, tab close, SSE loss, and a slow subscriber cancel only
  observation. They do not prove completion and do not cancel product work.
- On `recovery_required`, reconnect exhaustion, operation expiry, or a missing
  terminal event, follow the durable refresh link or run the equivalent CLI
  status/validation command before retrying.
- Explicit cancellation is idempotent. A late cancel cannot replace an already
  authoritative completion/failure result.
- During shutdown, new mutations receive `server_draining`; wait for the server
  to stop, inspect durable status, then restart and retry preparation.
- A `.cleanup-uncertain.json` marker means bounded shutdown could not prove
  cleanup. Restart reconciliation runs through the owning sprint/study module;
  process absence and artifact presence are evidence only, not success.
- A stale product mutation lock must be assessed through normal CLI status and
  lock guidance. Never delete it merely because the browser operation expired.

## Locks And `--force-unlock`

`run-loop` uses a per-study lock to refuse concurrent runs. Use:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> status
```

to inspect lock path, PID, command, and acquisition time.

Use `--force-unlock` only when an operator has confirmed the existing lock is stale:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> run-loop --force-unlock
```

Forcing an active lock can corrupt operator expectations, duplicate runtime work, and race report writes.

## Cancellation

On interrupt or context cancellation, the runtime boundary is asked to cancel and run state is preserved where possible. Recovery path:

1. Run `study status`.
2. Inspect cancelled or active tasks.
3. Run `study validate`.
4. Resume with `study run-loop` or rerun specific failed tasks.

## Retry And Fallback Metadata

Status output can include retry time, policy decisions, final attempt count, fallback decisions, repair metadata, cleanup metadata, usage, cost, and omitted raw payload notes. Use it to decide whether to wait for `retry_after`, fix runtime/provider config, or rerun after a provider issue clears.

Unknown usage or cost means the runtime did not provide safe metadata; it is not a validation failure by itself.

## Partial Completion

`run-all`, `run-loop`, and `code` can return partial completion when some work succeeded and some work failed or remained unresolved. Treat partial completion as release-blocking for production evidence unless the unresolved scope is explicitly documented.

## Failed Planning Stages

For a failed planning stage:

1. Run `ultraplan project <project> validate`.
2. Run `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> status`.
3. Validate the earliest incomplete stage with `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate <stage>`.
4. Use `prompt <stage>` to inspect the runtime input before rerunning flow.
5. Rerun `flow --to <stage>` only after the upstream artifact validates.

When using a stage skill, it performs the same checks and must ask before
filling prerequisite gaps. An explicit proposal-only or deep-dive discussion
does not advance flow state until the governed artifact is written and
validated.

Common causes are project-index references that do not resolve, sprint-index entries outside the project catalog, missing selected evidence, reasoning that does not include decisions/risks/evidence, or a plan that does not trace tasks to `reasoning.md`.

## Atomic Write Failures

UltraPlan writes durable state and generated artifacts loudly. If a write fails:

1. Preserve stderr and the failing path.
2. Check disk, permissions, parent directories, and workspace path safety.
3. Avoid manually editing run-state files unless directed by a focused remediation.
4. Re-run validation after filesystem issues are fixed.

## Read-only QA recovery

Start with `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> qa status --json` and inspect its phase, freshness reasons, map and implementation fingerprints, durable run correlation, blocker, cancellation, terminal result, and next action. Do not infer QA success from a run event or infer Conformance Review success from QA.

- `missing`: use `qa --dry-run`; recovery is a runtime-free no-op.
- `queued`, `running`, or `synthesizing` after process loss: run `qa recover`. It records `interrupted`, reconciles the bounded flow summary, and directs runtime work to `qa resume`.
- `stale`: inputs, implementation, Conformance Review evidence, policy, check catalog, limits, or selected shard no longer match. Run a new dry-run and start; never reuse stale outcomes as current.
- `invalid` or `unknown_schema`: stop. Keep the private state unchanged, use a compatible binary or documented migration, and do not hand-edit version or digest fields.
- `cancelled` or wall-clock exhaustion: completed promoted shards remain inspectable. Resume only if status says the semantic attempt is current.
- `cleanup_uncertain` or persistence failure: inspect the durable run and filesystem health, restore reliable local persistence, then recover. Do not claim completion.

Detailed records live under `projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/` with mode 0700 directories and 0600 files. `state.json` points to digest-checked records beneath `attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/`. A missing reference, digest mismatch, unsafe mode, symlink, path escape, malformed/trailing JSON, or unknown major version fails closed. Recovery can republish a previously validated terminal state to fix its `flow-state.json` summary; it never rebuilds missing theory evidence or adopts a worker.

Every resume accepts and claims a new durable run and fencing generation. A stale writer cannot publish. Cancellation cleanup uses a separate bounded context so the current owner can record truthful terminal state even after the work context is cancelled. If owner identity is lost, wait for run-control reconciliation and resume; never reuse a process or provider session.

Retention keeps at most eight semantic attempts by default, including the current protected attempt, and the detailed-state hard budget is 128 MiB. Normal start/recovery prunes only validated attempt directories in deterministic order. If quota is exhausted, preserve the current attempt, remove unrelated external files first, and use normal recovery; do not delete `state.json` or a referenced current directory manually.

A gated real-runtime QA run that cannot meet runtime, current evidence, local-filesystem, browser, or Git prerequisites is `blocked`. Record the missing prerequisite; fake-runtime tests do not satisfy the dogfood gate.

## Unsafe Data Handling

Do not paste provider tokens, full environment dumps, full prompts, full generated report bodies, or raw unsafe runtime payloads into issue reports or release evidence. Use redacted command summaries and artifact paths.
## Run-control recovery

Start with `ultraplan run diagnostics`, then inspect the affected run with
`ultraplan run show <run-id>` and replay retained evidence using
`ultraplan run follow <run-id> --after <sequence>`. A replay gap means earlier
events were compacted; refresh the snapshot and resume from its
`oldest_retained_sequence`. Never infer operational success from sprint/study
artifacts, a process ID, a lock, or a provider session.

Cancellation is a durable request, not proof that cleanup completed. States
such as `stalled`, `owner_unreachable`, `interrupted`, `cleanup_uncertain`, and
`persistence_degraded` intentionally preserve uncertainty. Re-run diagnostics,
confirm the exact process identity, and let reconciliation record a conservative
terminal outcome. Do not kill a PID based only on the number shown in support
evidence.

The private `.ultraplan/run-control.log` is bounded to 1 MiB and contains only
allowlisted structured correlation and decision fields. Prefer
`ultraplan run diagnostics --support-export <file>` to collect its newest safe
records with health, snapshots, omission facts, config source classes, and
reconciliation evidence. Do not substitute the log for the SQLite journal.

If a process exits after acceptance but before its first owner claim, the run
has no process identity to probe. After 45 seconds, reconciliation records an
`interrupted` terminal with `owner_never_claimed_after_grace`; it does not
invent an attempt or adopt any work that might remain outside run control.

For quota pressure, stop starting new work, free space outside the active
database, and rerun diagnostics. UltraPlan begins compaction at 80 percent,
rejects starts at the soft threshold, and reserves 16 MiB for heartbeat,
cancellation, recovery, and terminal writes. It never deletes an active
snapshot to regain space.

Schema migrations create private timestamped backups next to
`.ultraplan/run-control.db` (maximum three retained backups and 512 MiB per
backup). Restoration is an offline procedure: stop every UltraPlan process for
the workspace, keep the backup unchanged, restore the matching UltraPlan
binary, and use the tested restore path before reopening the workspace. Never
copy only the database while a WAL writer is active. An unsupported newer
schema or failed integrity check is a stop condition, not a fallback to an
empty history.

Run control is supported only for same-host processes on a local filesystem
with reliable SQLite locking/WAL semantics. Move the workspace to such a
filesystem before recovery if those guarantees are unavailable.

86: - `reconciliation required`: `smoke.md` committed but flow state did not. Validate both files and rerun smoke to reconcile; automatic recovery is deferred.

92: 
93: 1. Check whether an UltraPlan process is still running.
94: 2. Check lock diagnostics in `study status`.

96: 4. Resume with `study <study> run-loop` only after deciding the previous process is gone or safe to abandon. Continuing shared study progress is the default. Use `--reset` only when you intentionally want to archive and rebuild progress.

101: bounded, ephemeral views. Product-owned workspace/run state is authoritative.
102:

104:   observation. They do not prove completion and do not cancel product work.
105: - On `recovery_required`, reconnect exhaustion, operation expiry, or a missing
106:   terminal event, follow the durable refresh link or run the equivalent CLI
107:   status/validation command before retrying.
108: - Explicit cancellation is idempotent. A late cancel cannot replace an already
109:   authoritative completion/failure result.
110: - During shutdown, new mutations receive `server_draining`; wait for the server
111:   to stop, inspect durable status, then restart and retry preparation.
112: - A `.cleanup-uncertain.json` marker means bounded shutdown could not prove
113:   cleanup. Restart reconciliation runs through the owning sprint/study module;
114:   process absence and artifact presence are evidence only, not success.
115: - A stale product mutation lock must be assessed through normal CLI status and
116:   lock guidance. Never delete it merely because the browser operation expired.

139: 
140: 1. Run `study status`.
141: 2. Inspect cancelled or active tasks.
142: 3. Run `study validate`.

146:

161: 3. Validate the earliest incomplete stage with `ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate <stage>`.

166: filling prerequisite gaps. An explicit proposal-only or deep-dive discussion
167: does not advance flow state until the governed artifact is written and
168: validated.

175:

178: 3. Avoid manually editing run-state files unless directed by a focused remediation.

199:

201: 
202: Do not paste provider tokens, full environment dumps, full prompts, full generated report bodies, or raw unsafe runtime payloads into issue reports or release evidence. Use redacted command summaries and artifact paths.
203: ## Run-control recovery
204: 
205: Start with `ultraplan run diagnostics`, then inspect the affected run with
206: `ultraplan run show <run-id>` and replay retained evidence using
207: `ultraplan run follow <run-id> --after <sequence>`. A replay gap means earlier
208: events were compacted; refresh the snapshot and resume from its
209: `oldest_retained_sequence`. Never infer operational success from sprint/study
210: artifacts, a process ID, a lock, or a provider session.
211: 
212: Cancellation is a durable request, not proof that cleanup completed. States
213: such as `stalled`, `owner_unreachable`, `interrupted`, `cleanup_uncertain`, and
214: `persistence_degraded` intentionally preserve uncertainty. Re-run diagnostics,
215: confirm the exact process identity, and let reconciliation record a conservative
216: terminal outcome. Do not kill a PID based only on the number shown in support
217: evidence.

227: `interrupted` terminal with `owner_never_claimed_after_grace`; it does not

229: 
230: For quota pressure, stop starting new work, free space outside the active
231: database, and rerun diagnostics. UltraPlan begins compaction at 80 percent,
232: rejects starts at the soft threshold, and reserves 16 MiB for heartbeat,
233: cancellation, recovery, and terminal writes. It never deletes an active
234: snapshot to regain space.
235: 
236: Schema migrations create private timestamped backups next to
237: `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (maximum three retained backups and 512 MiB per
238: backup). Restoration is an offline procedure: stop every UltraPlan process for
239: the workspace, keep the backup unchanged, restore the matching UltraPlan
240: binary, and use the tested restore path before reopening the workspace. Never
241: copy only the database while a WAL writer is active. An unsupported newer
242: schema or failed integrity check is a stop condition, not a fallback to an
243: empty history.
244: 
245: Run control is supported only for same-host processes on a local filesystem
246: with reliable SQLite locking/WAL semantics. Move the workspace to such a
247: filesystem before recovery if those guarantees are unavailable.

(End of file - total 247 lines)
</content>

```text
                   [--lifecycle <comma-list>] [--limit <1..200>]
                   [--after <cursor>] [--json]
ultraplan run show <run-id> [--json]
ultraplan run follow <run-id> [--after <sequence>] [--json]
ultraplan run cancel <run-id> [--reason user_requested] [--json]
ultraplan run diagnostics [--json] [--support-export <file>]
```

`list` is newest-first, defaults to 50 records, and returns an opaque pagination
cursor. Active means only `accepted`, `queued`, `running`, or `cancelling`.
`follow` replays committed events, polls quickly while catching up and at most
once per second while idle. Interrupting follow stops observation only; use
`cancel` for an explicit durable cancellation command. Cancellation is
idempotent and does not overwrite an already-terminal winner.

Diagnostics reports schema/WAL, quota, retention, active/stalled ownership, and
reconciliation backlog. `--support-export` creates a private, bounded file (at
most 1 MiB) containing safe snapshots, event headers/omission facts, health,
config source classes, reconciliation decisions, and the newest sanitized
records from `.ultraplan/run-control.log`; it excludes event payloads, prompts,
provider data, source content, credentials, arbitrary output, and the absolute
workspace path.

216:`run-loop` persists shared study progress in `studies/<study>/.ultraplan/run-state.json` after meaningful task transitions, prints compact task progress as it runs, and refuses concurrent invocations through a per-study lock. By default, it resumes existing progress; dimension/source filters only choose which slice of the study graph is eligible to advance. On each start, it reconciles the persisted task graph against the current discovered source/dimension applicability so status totals and scheduling follow source metadata updates. It reads `dimension_order` on every invocation, so editing `study.json` changes the next scheduling decision without resetting durable progress.

reasoning_details.text:
I now have comprehensive coverage. Time to write the context pack to `review/surfaces/context-run-recovery-retention.md` following the established format (matching the sibling packs' structure). The pack must be neutral and descriptive — no defect claims.

Key content organization:

**Purpose**: Schema migration with backup/restore, stale-lock reclaim, crash reconciliation, event compaction/aging/tombstones, quota gates, support diagnostics export. Domain durability-core, risk high.

**Entrypoints/control flow**:
1. Open path: `OpenSQLite` (sqlite.go:60-134) → preparePrivateDatabase (154-191) → DSN pragmas → Ping → verifyPragmas (207-227) → migrateSchema (migration.go:25-82) → enforcePrivateMode → normalizeRetentionPolicy. Callers: app runControlState.repository (run_control.go:37-75; startup Reconcile after open), storage_commands.go:60 (storage migrate, default retention, no startup reconcile).
2. migrateSchema decision table:
   - version > 1 → ErrUnsupportedSchema (before lock)
   - version == 1 → verifySchemaRecord + integrityCheck only, no lock
   - version < 1 (0) → acquire migration lock (O_EXCL file `<db>.migrate.lock` 0600); re-read version under lock; if still 0 and hasApplicationSchema (any pre-existing non-sqlite_ objects) → checkpointWAL(TRUNCATE) then createMigrationBackup (≤512 MiB, .bak.<UTC nanosecond stamp>, O_EXCL 0600, fsync, remove-on-failure); then createInitialSchema (single tx: CREATE IF NOT EXISTS ×6 tables+trigger+indexes, app_schema record version=1, PRAGMA user_version=1); verifySchemaRecord; integrityCheck; pruneMigrationBackups (keep newest 3 by lexicographic name sort).
   - Lock acquisition: EEXIST → removeStaleMigrationLock reads JSON ProcessIdentity; malformed/legacy or Validate() fail → cannot authorize removal → CodeBusy retryable; probe PID: ErrProcessNotFound → proven gone → remove + retry acquire; other probe error → conservative keep → Busy; observed == expected → owner alive → Busy; mismatch → PID reuse proven → remove + retry.
   - Lock write: probe own identity first; failure → CodeUnavailable, removes lock file; writes JSON+\n, fsync, close; release = unlink.
3. RestoreBackup (migration.go:296-352): offline procedure. validateWorkspaceRoot; backupName must be base-name equal and prefixed `run-control.db.bak.`; Lstat regular non-symlink ≤512 MiB; validateBackupIntegrity opens read-only `_query_only=1` DSN and runs integrityCheck; CreateTemp in `.ultraplan/`, chmod 0600, copy bounded, fsync, close, rename over db, enforcePrivateMode. No CLI door — exported package function used by tests/runbook ("tested restore path").
4. Reconcile (lifecycle.go:301-416): grace default ReconciliationGrace=45s (negative invalid), limit default 64 max 256. Phase A unclaimed runs (terminal NULL, current_attempt NULL, accepted_at older than grace) ordered oldest-first → reconcileUnclaimed per-run immediate tx re-checks state, inserts terminal event without attempt_id, CAS UPDATE ... WHERE current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL → lifecycle interrupted, liveness terminal, proposed_by reconciler, reason owner_never_claimed_after_grace. Lost race → skip silently. recordReconciliation evidence rows {evidence: acceptance_timestamp_only}. Phase B expired-lease owners (JOIN attempts on current_attempt_id, lease_expires_at older than grace) → probe exact process birth: reconcileProcessDecision mapping: not found → interrupted; probe error → cleanup_uncertain; incomplete identity fields → cleanup_uncertain; mismatch (host/boot/pid/birth) → interrupted; exact live match → no outcome → markStalled (CAS on current_attempt + terminal NULL; lost → skip via ErrStaleFence/ErrTerminal continue). Terminal proposals go through ProposeTerminal with the stored fence (owner/generation from attempts row) so fencing arbitrates against a returned owner. recordReconciliation evidence {safe_identity_only} for attempt-backed decisions. finishReconciliationLog logs summary + increments metric.
   - Callers: startup at repository creation (app run_control.go:66), owner control loop every 10s (run_control.go:290), durableOperationManager every 10s (durable_operations.go:256).
5. Retention: normalizeRetentionPolicy (defaults 168h/720h/512 MiB; validation ≥1h, ≥24h & ≥full, ≥64 MiB & >16 MiB headroom). Compact(ctx, limit): limit 0→64 bounds 1..256; pressure = storageBytes ≥ 80% hard quota → compactCutoff = now else now - full/2. Stage 1: terminal runs record_state='full' finished_at ≤ cutoff → compactTerminalRun(RecordCompacted): delete progress/message/omission events; CAS UPDATE runs SET record_state/history_complete=0/oldest_retained_sequence=MIN(sequence)|last_sequence+1 WHERE terminal IS NOT NULL (changed != 1 → CodeConflict retryable). Stage 2: terminal runs 'full'|'compacted' finished_at ≤ now - full → tombstone: additionally deletes accepted/claimed/lifecycle/recovery events (keeps warning/finding/artifact/cancellation/terminal). Note TombstonedRuns incremented even when deleted==0. Stage 3: DELETE tombstone runs terminal finished_at ≤ now-full-tombstone ORDER BY finished_at LIMIT batch; then wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) + incremental_vacuum(64) errors ignored; log + metrics.compactions.
   - Per-run inline compaction compactRunJournal during Append (sqlite.go:687): up to 32 batches of ≤256 deletions of oldest progress/message/omission preserving current sequence; recomputes boundary; if nothing removable while over caps → CodeQuota "required durable event history reached its bounded capacity".
   - Quota gates: Accept pre-flight storageBytes ≥80% hard quota → Compact(64) once then re-measure; ≥ softQuota (hard −16 MiB) → CodeQuota retryable accept_quota. Append: ≥ hard quota and non-reserved type → CodeQuota retryable append_quota (reserved types: lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission). Heartbeat: ≥ hard quota → CodeQuota heartbeat_quota requires stop.
   - storageBytes sums sizes of all regular files in .ultraplan whose names start with "run-control.db" — includes db, -wal, -shm AND backups (.bak.*) and any fixture files sharing prefix.
6. Support export entrypoint: run diagnostics --support-export (run_commands.go:230-377): described already in sibling pack but this surface owns it per assignment. Health() reads pragmas, counts, backlog predicates using julianday('now') when wall clock / injected-clock comparisons; storageBytes; status ok/degraded/failed; LocalMetrics snapshot. writeRunSupportExport: List(50), config trio + source classes, ReconciliationEvidence(100) via anonymous interface assertion, ReadLocalLogs(root,100), per-run Events(runID,0,50) reduced to headers (payload excluded), MarshalIndent, >1 MiB reject, O_CREATE|O_EXCL 0600, fsync, remove-on-failure. Envelope status = health.Status for --json.

**Local log**: OpenLocalFileLogger — Lstat dir/log symlink rejection, O_APPEND 0600, enforcePrivateMode verify. Log(): message safeEventValue 256; fields key ≤64 non-sensitive else skipped; unsafe/oversize value → "[omitted]"; marshal; >4 KiB drop silently; stat size check +1 MiB cap drop-later; single append write. ReadLocalLogs(limit 1..500): symlink/oversize/nonregular → CodeCorrupt; scanner buffer 4 KiB; malformed lines skipped; sliding window keeps newest N.

**Sanitize**: sanitizeEventDraft allowlist ~35 fields; sensitive fragment deny list (adds prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command to credential markers); unsafeEventValue: control chars \x00\r\n, absolute paths (filepath.IsAbs + Windows drive letter pattern), credential markers bearer/sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/-----begin private key; oversize allowed detail replaced by EventWarning code=event_detail_oversize; MaxEncodedEventBytes 128 KiB fallback replacement; mergeOmission accounting; safeEventValue strips NUL/CR/LF + TrimSpace + byte-truncation (may split UTF-8 rune).

**Inputs/outputs**, **authoritative state**, **invariants**, **trust boundaries** (corrupt/hostile DB must not be silently replaced — test-pinned; lock file contents parsed as identity proof; local trust model; export contents), **external effects & cancellation/retry/restart semantics**, **dependencies** (run-journal-fencing owns sqlite.go internals/fencing; durable-operation-spine; product-state-mirror via storage migrate; cli-dispatch-exit-contract; web/tui consume same pool; config-inspection-health), **contracts** (recovery.md run-control recovery section; cli-reference diagnostics; TRD lines; configuration.md retention keys; user-guide), **tests evidence map**, **unknowns**.

Unknowns I noticed (neutral phrasing, no judgments):
1. Backup naming sorts lexicographically (`sort.Strings`) — timestamp format 20060102T150405.000000000Z is fixed-width so lexicographic == chronological within UTC; clock changes could reorder; also two backups in same nanosecond collide (O_EXCL fails → migration aborts).
2. createMigrationBackup copies only the main DB file after TRUNCATE checkpoint; WAL/SHM not copied; checkpoint busy → abort. If another process opens the DB between checkpoint and copy... (that's reviewer territory; describe mechanism: lock only serializes migrators, not ordinary openers — comment at migration.go:33-35 states the lock protects schema writes not startup).
3. RestoreBackup does not remove or archive the existing -wal/-shm files before rename-over; describe as fact: rename replaces main db file while stale WAL sidecars may exist next to it. Hmm — is that a defect? It's an observation; recovery.md says "Never copy only the database while a WAL writer is active" and requires stopping all processes. After clean stop, WAL may still contain frames? On clean close SQLite checkpoints and deletes WAL. RestoreBackup doesn't itself open the target db, so leftover WAL from a crashed writer would be applied to the restored db on next open. This is a factual mechanism worth listing under unknowns neutrally: "RestoreBackup replaces only run-control.db; pre-existing run-control.db-wal/-shm files are neither removed nor validated by the restore path; whether a stale WAL can be applied to a restored image depends on prior crash state — unannotated."
4. hasApplicationSchema counts ANY user object (table/index/trigger) — a hostile/random file that happens to parse as SQLite with one table triggers backup; conversely empty-but-valid db gets no backup. Also version==0 with hasSchema false skips backup entirely (fresh db).
5. integrity_check on every open of a current-version database (cost on every command; large dbs). Neutral performance note.
6. Migration lock identity: probeNativeProcess(context.Background()) ignores caller ctx — cancellation during lock acquisition/probe is not honored. Neutral fact.
7. acquireMigrationLock retries once after stale removal; concurrent reclaimers could both observe stale and both attempt O_EXCL; loser gets Busy. Fine.
8. Lock release closure unconditionally os.Remove(path) — could delete another process's lock if this process's release races after its own lock was reclaimed as stale... wait can that happen? The lock contains THIS process's identity; another process would find observed==expected (alive) → won't reclaim. But if this process hangs (SIGSTOP) beyond... probe returns alive → no removal. If this process exits, release never runs anyway. Edge: PID reuse where a different process now has our recorded identity — impossible since birth token matches only us while we live. OK, but note: the release func removes by path without verifying ownership at removal time (TOCTOU between stale-reclaim and original owner's release is guarded by identity check, since reclaimers refuse while owner alive). Neutral unknown: none really. Skip.
9. Compaction stage 2 tombstone: report.TombstonedRuns++ regardless of deleted>0 — double-processing across stages (a run compacted in stage 1 becomes candidate for tombstone in stage 2 within same pass if finished_at ≤ full-history cutoff). Factual control-flow note.
10. Compact deletes events by type lists; tombstone keeps warning/finding/artifact/cancellation/terminal events forever until expiry — factual.
11. storageBytes includes .bak.* backups and quota-fixture-like files in quota math — backups count toward workspace quota (and thus can trigger soft/hard gates). Recovery.md says "free space outside the active database" — hmm, actually it says free space outside; backups are inside the counted set. Neutral observation for reviewers.
12. Quota checks are TOCTOU-prone by design (measure-then-write); SQLITE_FULL backstop typed as Quota retryable.
13. Health backlog predicate uses julianday('now') (SQLite connection clock) vs injected clock comparisons — dual time authorities documented in comment.
14. Reconcile phase ordering: unclaimed processed first, remaining budget limits expired-owner scan; batch cap means backlog drains over multiple passes (10 s cadence).
15. markStalled sets liveness='stalled' but does NOT write a reconciliation_log row unless recordReconciliation called afterward — it is (line 411 records for both actions).
16. recordReconciliation errors are discarded (`_ =`) — evidence loss possible while decision persists. Neutral fact.
17. ProposeTerminal by reconciler uses stored fence; if owner came back alive and heartbeated between scan and propose, CAS fails → skipped (won=false) but evidence row still written claiming action terminal_proposal even when not won — factual: report.Decisions appended regardless of won.
18. Support export: List limit 50 — runs beyond newest 50 have no events/snapshots in export. Silent truncation. Already noted in sibling pack unknown #5; keep brief here with cross-ref.
19. runDiagnostics re-runs discovery/config inside support branch (already sibling unknown #6) — mention briefly.
20. ReadLocalLogs sliding window: when len(records)==limit it copies left then appends → keeps last `limit`; correct-ish; note off-by-one? copy(records, records[1:]) shifts; then records[:limit-1]; append → length limit. Fine.
21. sanitize safeEventValue truncates bytes possibly splitting multibyte runes — persisted value may be invalid UTF-8; JSON marshal of invalid UTF-8 replaces with U+FFFD. Neutral.
22. LocalFileLogger.Log drops records when file stat fails or size exceeded — silent drop by design (comment documents).
23. Migration: `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` busy != 0 → abort with Busy retryable — migration cannot proceed while other connections hold the WAL. Multi-process open of legacy db contends.
24. user_version vs app_schema dual versioning must stay consistent; verifySchemaRecord enforces equality post-migration.
25. RestoreBackup validates backup integrity read-only but does NOT verify schema version of the backup — restoring a v99 backup? integrity_check passes (physical integrity) — then next open fails unsupported-schema. Actually that's fine behavior-wise (fail-closed). Neutral note.
26. Export asserts nothing about excluding workspace path at runtime (test-only guarantee). Sibling covered.
27. `Compact` is only reachable via Accept's quota-pressure branch (and tests) — there is no periodic or CLI-triggered compaction pass; tombstone/expiry aging therefore happens only when new accepts hit 80% pressure. Wait — is that right? grep showed Compact called only from sqlite.go:387 (Accept) and retention_test. So yes: aging-to-tombstone and expiry occur solely inside the Accept quota-pressure path (or direct API callers e.g., future web?). Let me double check RunUseCases — does web expose compaction? RunUseCases = Runs/Run/RunEvents/CancelRun/RunHealth — no Compact. So the ONLY production trigger of retention aging is Accept-time pressure. That's a significant descriptive fact about control flow (not judging). Also note Accept triggers Compact only when usage ≥80% hard quota; otherwise terminal runs age never. Hmm wait — also check durable_operations.go for Compact usage... grep found none. Correct.

Also entrypoints say "internal/app/run_commands.go:support export" — covered.

Surface dependency: run-journal-fencing (critical) — shares files: sqlite.go/lifecycle.go/model.go/id.go/process*.go; this surface's assigned primary paths are migration.go, retention.go, local_log.go, sanitize.go (+ Reconcile slice of lifecycle.go + support export slice of run_commands.go). State overlap noted.

Also import_boundary_test pins runcontrol deps to stdlib + modernc.org/sqlite + golang.org/x/sys/unix.
